target_customer: Post-sales teams (customer success, forward deployed and customer engineers) at companies with usage-based pricing
problem: After a deal closes, onboarding, adoption and renewals are handled manually across CRM, billing and support tools, so launches take weeks and expansion and risk signals are missed.
business_model: B2B SaaS with AI agents; pricing not published
product_category: AI agents for post-sales and customer success

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that read CRM, billing, support and Slack signals and act on them need many integrations and reliability work, built on existing models.

defensibility.rationale: Customer history and workflows in the product create some lock-in, but every established customer success vendor added agents by mid 2026.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents shipped agent features during 2026 (Gainsight Atlas, ChurnZero Agentic Essentials, OnRamp Aero).

market_need_then: Usage-based pricing is spreading (the CMU spotlight, reflecting company messaging, says 85 percent of software companies have or plan it), making account health and expansion tracking more urgent.

branding.domain_note: Uses quivly.ai; the YC slug quivly-ai suggests quivly.com was not available, but no source states this.

identity.visual_style: Modular product site with before and after sections
identity.voice_and_tone: Bold, concise, results-oriented, speaks to you about your pain points.

brand_strength.rationale: Invented -ly name with no explanation; searches mix it up with QuiverAI, Quivr and Quikly.

outcome_analysis: Quivly is a Fall 2026 YC company founded in 2024 by two experienced product and fintech operators, selling post-sales agents. It is too early for an outcome. The incumbents all added agents in 2026, so Quivly must differentiate on usage-based pricing customers and execution speed.

The grant is recorded only as other with amount unknown and rests on one aggregator; treat as low certainty.
